content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-8|COREMERCH guide to payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/github-pages-free-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-digital-product-payment-solutions-west-africa-works|How Digital]]-product-store-hosting-explained-3|github]] Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Platform stripe

The ban on digital platforms like Stripe and PayPal is not a one-time event, but a recurring reality for creators in restricted countries. This phenomenon is not limited to Stripe; other popular platforms like Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle also restrict or ban accounts in certain countries. The consequences of these bans can be severe, with creators losing access to their funds, data, and customer base. The infrastructure problem here is not just a matter of platform availability, but a fundamental question of sovereignty and control over one's digital presence.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The solution to this infrastructure problem lies in sovereign commerce infrastructure, which provides a permanent structural alternative to traditional digital platforms. This architecture is based on a combination of free and paid tools, including GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase, Google Drive, NOWPayments, and Google Sheets. The beauty of this solution lies in its decentralization and modularity, allowing creators to maintain full control over their digital presence, data, and funds.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This solution is specifically designed for digital creators in countries where traditional platforms like Stripe and PayPal are unavailable or severely restricted. This includes countries like Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Cameroon, Tanzania, and the Philippines. The goal of this solution is to empower creators in these countries to build and maintain their digital presence without relying on external platforms.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a permanent structural alternative to traditional digital platforms.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is a key component of this solution, providing a fully functional e-commerce stack that includes Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments. This stack is designed to be scalable, secure, and easy to use, with features like SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured from the start. The NOWPayments integration allows for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, eliminating the need for third-party payment processors.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy this solution today, follow these concrete steps. First, sign up for a GitHub account and create a new repository for your e-commerce site. Next, deploy the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) and customize it to suit your needs. Finally, integrate NOWPayments and set up automatic payment verification. By following these steps, you can build a sovereign e-commerce presence that is not beholden to any external platform.
